svg.title: Looking back and looking ahead
svg.desc: Original family-manga illustration: magnifier, related to Looking back and looking ahead.

text.tspan: A good way to make a realistic plan combines practical structure with an awareness of other people. Neither a rigid
plan nor complete improvisation is sufficient on its own; both need to be judged in context.
The practical case is straightforward: reviewing a specific experience teaches more than a vague judgement. Consider how we describe one habit that
helped us instead of calling the whole year good or bad. The benefit is not merely efficiency. A modest arrangement prevents avoidable confusion,
leaving attention available for the activity itself rather than for problems that could have been anticipated.
Consideration adds a second, equally important dimension: a small next step is easier to act on than a broad promise. In this situation, we choose a
ten-minute practice session and put it on the calendar. A decision can be convenient for one person while creating difficulty for another, so its value
depends partly on whose needs it recognises.
The most useful approach therefore brings structure and consideration together. Preparation establishes a workable starting point; attention to other
people keeps it responsive. Success should be assessed by how well the arrangement serves the experience, rather than by how closely events follow
BUILD YOUR OWN · State a focused main idea. Develop one supporting reason in each body paragraph, with a concrete example. Conclude by connecting the two
reasons without introducing a new argument. Use the structure as a model; write about an experience of your own.
Review without reading the example first. What two reasons support the main idea? Explain one example.
